entries.source: Excerpt from Everything and Nothing by D Everyman On quantum consciousness Experimentally, we can capture the full material state of a single brain over a succession of contiguous quantised time intervals, resulting in a digitised 'recording' of a consciousness stream. In theory, if such a capture were conducted over an entire lifetime, we would obtain a full recording of an entity's consciousness stream. In practice, however, the storage capacity required to represent such a recording over a non-trivial time-period proves too vast, not to mention the logisitcal difficulties in carrying out the actual recording. So instead we capture discrete brain states (we call them ego-dumps), at different times, possibly several hours apart and interpolate the set of intermediate states in real-time, on demand. In so doing, we sacrifice fidelity, but the data-loss is not fatal, and we are able to arrive at a reasonable approximation of the full capture for a fraction of the storage.
entries.translation: 节选自 D·埃弗里曼所著一切与虚无 论量子意识 在实验中，我们可以在一连串连续的量子化时间间隔内，完整捕捉单个大脑的物质状态，从而生成意识流的数字化“记录”。 理论上，若这种捕捉能够贯穿一个生命体的整个人生，我们就能获得该实体意识流的完整记录。 但在实践中，要在有实际意义的长周期内呈现如此庞大的记录，所需存储容量过于巨大，更不用说在实施实际记录时所面临的后勤困难了。 因此，我们改为在不同时间点（可能相隔数小时）捕捉离散的大脑状态（我们称之为自我转储），并根据需求实时插补一系列中间状态。 这样一来，我们虽然牺牲了保真度，但数据损失并非致命，而且我们能以极小一部分的存储空间，换取对完整记录的合理近似。

entries.source: Excerpt from Everything and Nothing by D Everyman On connectivity A post-matter ego cannot have direct recollection of its own material death. Post-matter egos therefore believe themselves materially alive until sufficient evidence to the contrary assimilates, the amount of evidence being in direct proportion to the legacy belief system quotient of the pre-death ego. Just as we can record periodic ego-dumps during a sentient entity's material life, we can continue to record ego-dumps throughout post-matter existence. This means we can interpolate from material to post-material conscious experience, re-restore the connected ego-streams, and the redeemed entity can in some sense then be said to have experienced its own death.
entries.translation: 节选自 D·埃弗里曼所著一切与虚无 论连通性 后物质自我无法直接回忆起自身的物质死亡。 因此，后物质自我也就自认为在肉体上依然存活，直到有充分的反面证据被其同化吸收为止；而所需证据的多少，与生前自我的遗留信念系统商数成正比。 正如我们可以在有感知实体的物质生命期间定期记录自我转储一样，我们也可以在整个后物质存在阶段继续记录自我转储。 这意味着我们可以在物质与后物质意识体验之间进行插值，重新恢复相连的自我流，而在某种意义上，重获新生的实体便可以说是亲历了自己的死亡。

entries.source: Excerpt from Everything and Nothing by D Everyman On Schrodinger's CAT It is not so much a question of whether or not the CAT is dead or alive before the drawer is opened, but more a question of whether or not the CAT can be the thing that is found, irrespective of where it has been concealed. To put it another way: If I secrete a little CAT in a drawer, and that CAT is later to be found, the finder cannot know they have found it unless they have prior knowledge that there was in fact a findable to be found.
entries.translation: 节选自 D·埃弗里曼所著一切与虚无 论薛定谔的CAT 问题并不在于打开抽屉之前CAT究竟是死是活，而在于无论CAT被藏在何处，它本身是否能成为“被找到的事物”。 换句话说：如果我把一只小CAT藏进抽屉里，而后这只CAT被找到了，那么寻找者若非事先知晓实际上存在一个“可寻之物”，便根本不可能知道自己已经找到了它。

James.

詹姆斯。

At this stage I cannot divulge the overarching goal of Project Buttercup, but have trust, friends: You are contributing to something truly great.

各位将被分配到专门负责某项特定专业开发任务的子团队中。
在现阶段，我还无法透露“毛茛项目”的终极目标，但请坚信，朋友们：你们正在为一项真正伟大的事业添砖加瓦。

entries.source: Project Buttercup is classified under protocol 42, and therefore I don't need to remind you that no information pertaining to or arising from your assignment is to be disclosed beyond the confines of the technical laboratory.

entries.source:

Your MUM will screen all access to enforce zero project asset leakage and zero security transgressions.
entries.translation:

你的MUM将对所有进出进行筛查，以确保项目资产零泄露、安全违规零发生。

entries.source:
Given the importance of your work, you will each be required to make a minimum 6 brain dumps per session.
This is primarily to ensure we always have a good working backup version of you, but it also gives us the opportunity to examine your stream to detect any counter-compliance that could jeopardise the project.
entries.translation:
鉴于各位工作的重要性，每个人每班次必须进行至少 6 次大脑转储。
这主要是为了确保我们始终保有你运转良好的备份版本，同时也为我们提供了审查你意识流的机会，以侦测出任何可能危及项目的违规倾向。

entries.source:
I am pleased to report that team Daisy has made significant progress with the ether-kinematic propulsion system.
For the uninitiated, this technology will enable us to construct ego-carrier devices capable of auto-navigating the consciousness ctrl stream, somewhat analogously to free-flight.
This is a truly thrilling development that should fill you with unashamed glee.
entries.translation:
我很高兴地宣布，雏菊团队在以太动能推进系统方面取得了重大进展。
对于外行而言，这项技术将使我们能够建造一种自我载体设备，该设备能够在意识Ctrl流中自主导航，某种程度上类似于自由飞行。
这真是一项激动人心的进展，应当让各位满怀毫无保留的欣喜。

entries.source:
Team Dandylion has succeeded in developing a fully functional virtual version of the Everyman sensor - i.e. an ethermatic sensor.
The new sensor can be detected by EMUs, but is entirely invisible to the human eye. 
The truly exciting breakthrough is that the new sensor can be mounted to ego-carrier devices, meaning that we are closer than ever to achieving a hostable 'ghost' carrier.
entries.translation:
蒲公英团队已成功研发出埃弗里曼传感器的全功能虚拟版本——即以太传感器。
新传感器可被EMU探测到，但肉眼完全无法察觉。
真正令人振奋的突破在于，这种新传感器可以安装在自我载体设备上，这意味着我们比以往任何时候都更接近实现可供自我寄宿的“幽灵”载体。

entries.source:
Outstanding development!
We now have a working prototype of a primary ego-carrier add-on that enables the host to 'extract' ego from a secondary carrier without the necessity of subsuming it, with zero ego fragmentation, and leaving the secondary ego partially intact!
In theory this means we can grow massive egos by 'borrowing' ego from several secondary carriers, use the massive ego to solve problems, and then return the ego to the secondary carriers after use.
entries.translation:
突破性进展！
我们现在拥有了一个可运行的主自我载体附加组件原型。它使宿主能够从次级载体中“提取”自我，而无需将其吞并吸收，自我碎片化为零，并能让次级自我保持部分完好！
理论上，这意味着我们可以通过向数个次级载体“借用”自我来培育出极其庞大的自我，利用庞大的自我来解决问题，并在使用完毕后将自我归还给次级载体。

entries.source:
David Everyman has done it again!
He's demonstrated that by continuously serializing and deserializing CRS-treated ethermatical objects in real-time, faster than the eye can perceive, you can actually make physical objects appear to shift around, as if by 'magic'.
He did this in an afternoon. 
The man's a genius and we salute him.
entries.translation:
大卫·埃弗里曼又立奇功！
他证明了：只要以快过肉眼察觉的速度，实时、持续地序列化与反序列化经过CRS处理的以太质物体，你就能真正让物理实体仿佛“施了魔法”一般四处移位变换。
他只花了一个下午就搞定了这个。
此人真是个天才，向他致敬。

entries.source:
Team Bindweed have adapted a bug chassis to incorporate a fuel resevoir, filled it with the industrial solvent found in regular packets of juice, and demonstrated that burning the juice under void conditions is sufficient to power several ethermatic functions.
They've even built a placeholder EMU readout. 
Well done boys! 
(And Pamela)
entries.translation:
旋花小队（Team Bindweed）改装了一个BUG底盘，在其中加入了一个燃料箱，里面装满了普通动力液包装里常见的那种工业溶剂；他们已经证实，在虚空条件下燃烧动力液足以驱动若干项以太质功能。
他们甚至还做出了一个EMU读数占位界面。
干得好，小伙子们！
（还有帕梅拉）

entries.source:
Team Ivy have produced an early prototype of a tight-pocket ethermatic wave implosion. 
The implosion doesn't actually happen in what we think of as the real world, but instead implodes ethermaterially, destroying information, including ego, which can in turn cause ego-death, which impacts real-world host integrity, thereby creating the illusion that an implosion event has in fact occurred in what we think of as the real world.
entries.translation:
常春藤小队（Team Ivy）研制出了紧缩囊袋以太波内爆的早期原型。
这种内爆实际上并不会发生在我们所认为的现实世界中，而是在以太质层面上发生内爆，摧毁包括自我在内的信息，进而导致自我消亡，从而影响现实世界中宿主的完整性——由此营造出一种错觉，仿佛在我们所认为的现实世界中确实发生了一场内爆事件。

entries.source:
We dared to dream.
We dared to imagine a world where everything is information.
We dared to fabricate digitised consciousnesses from the post-mattter brain dumps of our fellow humans.
We dared to write software that executes invisibly and immaterially in the ether-wave residue of the consciousness ctrl stream.
We dared to embark on Project Buttercup.
And, friends: We are close. So close.

我们敢于构想梦想。
我们敢于设想一个万物皆为信息的世界。
我们敢于用同胞们后物质时代的脑部转储数据，制造出数字化意识。
我们敢于编写无形且非物质的代码，使其在意识ctrl流的以太波残余中隐匿运行。
我们敢于启动毛茛计划。
而现在，朋友们：我们接近了。如此接近。

Hello David.

You were right - this thing is extremely dangerous.

I observed it suck the consciousness out from my lab assistant, a truly horrible spectacle.

It already had a large ego and there appears to be no upper limit on how large it can grow.

The consequences of that thing getting out in the wild are just unimaginable.

So yes, you were definitely right.

Project buttercup must be stopped at any cost.

那东西一旦流窜到外面的世界，后果不堪设想。

entries.source:
David,

I have some information that might help you if you decide to terminate The Executor, assuming he's still around when you return. If you return.

I heard The Executor intends to have a welcoming party ready for you. Let's face it - it's not likely to be a very welcoming welcome party.

But if you can remain undetected up on the Corporate floor, even though he'll know you're coming he won't know WHEN you're coming. I think you'd stand a good chance of catching him unawares - it might even be possible to terminate him without having to confront him at all.

I've been looking at the schematics and there are a number of ceiling vents above the Corporate offices that may help.

I hope this information proves helpful. I'm sorry I couldn't be here to assist you. 

Good luck, my love.

PAM.
entries.translation:
大卫：

如果你决定终结执行者，我这里有些信息或许能帮到你——假设你回来时他还在的话。如果你还能回来的话。

我听说执行者打算为你准备一场欢迎会。实话说——这多半不会是一场热情的欢迎会。

但如果你能在行政区保持隐蔽，即便他知道你要来，也不会知道你【何时】到来。我认为你很有机会杀他个措手不及——甚至有可能完全不用正面对抗就能终结他。

我查阅了结构图，行政区办公室上方有若干天花板通风管道，或许能派上用场。

希望这些信息能帮上忙。很抱歉我无法留在这里协助你。

祝你好运，亲爱的。

PAM

entries.source:
Ego-Sucker tool notes v6.18

Disclaimer: Users of the tool should bear in mind the moral implications of consuming ego from other sentient entities. Remember: they were people once too.

• Any ego-bearing host sensor may be targeted

• Ego is extracted through target sensors in discrete packets, or fragments

• Owing to egomatic convergence, it may be possible to extract through glass - see WORM user guide.

• Ego extraction requires an energy source, e.g. a BUG equipped with a juice exchanger

• Ego extraction is mostly painless and in modest quantities, barely detectable

• Lengthy extractions can cause discomfort and are not recommended

entries.source:
Dear The Conscious Robot Services Science Department,

I am writing to you to raise a critical health and safety concern regarding your ethermaterial canister containers.

The concern is that under experimental conditions we were able to reproduce reliably a state whereby faulting canisters became dangerously volatile.

In this state, the canisters are liable to implode with overwhelming severity, representing a significant peril to both material and post-matter entities alike.

I hope you will take this constructive feedback with the seriousness it deserves and take remedial measures to secure your canisters for safer storage.

Many thanks,

Jones
@GOD's workshop
entries.translation:
致 有意识机器人服务公司科学部：

我谨致信向贵部提出一项关于以太物质储存罐的关键健康与安全隐患。

问题在于，在实验条件下，我们已能稳定重现故障储存罐变得极度不稳定的状态。

在此状态下，储存罐极易发生剧烈内爆，对实体物质与后物质形态的存在均构成重大威胁。

希望贵部能高度重视此项建设性反馈，并采取补救措施，以确保储存罐安全存放。

顺祝商祺，

琼斯
@GOD的车间

entries.source: Excerpt from Everything and Nothing by D Everyman On Recollection Memory is fragile, fallible, and prone to a high degree of interpretive error and cognitive consonance. Yet we depend on it to define who we are and to frame our system of beliefs. Given its vulnerability, it's a wonder any of us are able to take ourselves seriously at all.
entries.translation: 节选自D·埃弗里曼所著一切与虚无 论回忆 记忆脆弱、不可靠，且极易出现高度的解读偏差与认知一致性。 然而，我们却依赖它来定义自己是谁，构筑我们的信仰体系。 鉴于其脆弱性，我们竟然还能一本正经地看待自己，简直是个奇迹。

entries.source:
Hi Mrs Bosswoman,

The exec wants all access to science and corporate sealed off - I think he fears another parasite attack.

I'm working through the access points - will update you when I'm done.

entries.translation:

执行者想要封锁所有通往科学部和行政区的通道——我觉得他是怕再遭到寄生虫袭击。

我正在挨个处理各处出入通道——弄完后会向你汇报最新进展。

• 停用电梯——已完成

• 封锁前楼梯——已完成

• 封锁后楼梯——处理中——在我回头处理这事之前，我先把行政区后门锁上了，密钥特征附在这封消息后。

entries.source:
The Executor has denied all access to the science lab.
Even David has been banned.
I've always trusted the exec, but this virus thing is really starting to worry me.
I can't quite put my finger on it, but something doesn't seem quite right about feeding it the minds of our former colleagues.
entries.translation:
执行者拒绝了所有进入科学实验室的权限。
就连大卫也被禁了。
我一直都很信任执行者，但这个病毒玩意儿真的开始让我担心了。
我也说不太准，但拿我们前同事的心智去喂它，感觉总有点不对劲。

entries.source:
David? 
Is that you?
Have you come back like you said you would?
entries.translation:
大卫？
是你吗？
你照你说的回来了吗？

entries.source:
The access door to Oversight is complaining about being bored again.
To be fair, I have to admit I don't particularly fancy being brought back as a door.
Poor Jeff.
entries.translation:
通往监察部的通行门又在抱怨无聊了。
平心而论，不得不说，我可不太想被转生成一扇门。
可怜的杰夫。

entries.source:
Fingerprint scanner for POD C is on the blink again.
I've set it to accept a 2-part virtual fingerprint until I get time to look properly.
Come see me for details.
entries.translation:
C舱的指纹扫描仪又出毛病了。
在有时间彻底检修之前，我把它设成了接受双段虚拟指纹。
详情来找我面谈。

entries.source:
Here's the fingerprint key for POD D.
David asked me to leave it here, but as usual he didn't bother to explain why.
entries.translation:
这是D舱的指纹密钥。
大卫让我留在这儿的，但跟平时一样，他根本懒得解释为什么。

entries.source:
Received a strange call out of the blue from David this morning.
He wants me to leave a copy of his favourite bug tool program along with his favourite bug.
So that he'd know where to look for it when he comes back, he said.
I asked him where he was going, and he said 'everywhere and nowhere', which I suppose he thinks is funny, that being the title of his book 'n all.
entries.translation:
今天早上突然接到大卫打来的奇怪电话。
他想让我把他最喜欢的BUG工具程序和最喜欢的BUG留在一起。
他说这样一来，等他回来时就知道该去哪儿找了。
我问他要去哪儿，他说“无所不在，又无处可寻”，我猜他自以为这很幽默，毕竟那是他的书名嘛。

entries.source:
The Executor has asked me to clone the virus thing.
I don't know what to do.
Surely he must know that would be illegal!?
But after what happened to David, I fear I have no choice but to go along with it.
I desperately need to find a way out of here.
entries.translation:
执行者要求我克隆那个病毒玩意儿。
我不知道该怎么办。
他肯定知道这是违法的吧！？
但大卫出事之后，我恐怕别无选择，只能顺着他来。
我必须得想办法离开这里。

entries.source:
I still can't believe Martin had his brain sucked dry by that thing.
I've tried calling David but he's not answering.
So I've sealed the door to POD B.
GOD help us.
entries.translation:
我还是不敢相信马丁的大脑居然被那东西吸干了。
我试着给大卫打电话，但他没接。
所以我把B舱的门封死了。
愿上帝保佑我们。

entries.source:
Yesterday, on a routine trip through the roof of POD B, I had the unnerving feeling that the virus thing was sensing me through my pup eyes.
I got out of there pronto - really creepy.
entries.translation:
昨天，在例行穿越B舱顶部时，我产生了一种令人不安的感觉，仿佛那个病毒玩意儿正通过我的PUP之眼感知着我。
我立马溜之大吉——真叫人毛骨悚然。

entries.source:
I'm finding David's shift program incredibly useful, sort of feels like having weird strength.
It works through glass too, which is even weirder, but means I can do much of my work without even having to enter the pods.
entries.translation:
我发现大卫的移位程序出奇的好用，感觉就像拥有了某种不可思议的怪力。
它甚至能穿透玻璃起效，这就更诡异了，但也意味着我甚至不用进舱就能搞定大部分工作。

entries.source:
Virus:
A disembodied entity capable of growing its ego and ctrling other ego-bearing entities.
The consequences of one of these things ever getting out... are unimaginable.
entries.translation:
病毒：
一种无实体的存在，能够壮大自身自我并ctrl其他具有自我的实体。
一旦让这类东西跑出去……后果将不堪设想。

entries.source:
This virus thing is definitely dangerous, despite the assurances of The Executor.
And it's not at all like buttercups, which are cute and yellow.
entries.translation:
尽管有执行者的再三保证，但这病毒玩意儿绝对很危险。
而且它一点也不像毛茛花——人家又可爱又黄澄澄的。

entries.source:
David? 

It's really you? 

I've hidden the key to your bug where only you could find it, just as you asked me. 

At the accident site.

I've rigged it so that it only responds to you.
entries.translation:
大卫？

真的是你吗？

我已经按你的要求，把你的BUG钥匙藏到了只有你能找到的地方。

就在事故现场。

我动了手脚，让它只对你起反应。

entries.source:
David?

There's a problem.

You said that if the worst happens, you'd try to use a temporary version of yourself to bring yourself back. But The Executor has deleted your ego backup history as far back as when you first began to question him, so even if your plan works, you'll still not remember any of it.

There's still a chance though:

I managed to bootleg your last ego backup onto disk before The Executor purged the repository. I put the disk in a PUP and dispatched the PUP to The Cloud.

So if you're here, go there. To the Cloud. Find yourself.

PAM.

PS. FYEO Here's half the POD C fingerprint. The other half is on my eye-pad - my assistant borrowed it - look under POD B.
entries.translation:
大卫？

出问题了。

你说过如果情况变得最糟，你会尝试用一个临时的自己来让自己复活。但执行者已经删除了你自从开始质疑他以来的自我备份历史。所以就算你的计划成功，你也仍然不会记得这段经历。

不过还有一个机会：

在执行者清理库之前，我设法把你的最后一份自我备份私自刻录到了磁盘上。我把磁盘放进了一台PUP，并把那台PUP送到了“云端”。

所以如果你到了这里，就去那里吧。去云端。找回你自己。

PAM。

又及：仅供你亲阅。这是舱室 C指纹的一半。另一半在我的EyePad 平板上——我助手借走了它——去舱室 B下面找找。

entries.source:
Oh David

They took me upstairs

Opened me up

Inspected me

I've never felt so humiliated

I hope you really do return

Impossible as that seems
entries.translation:
噢，大卫

他们把我带到了楼上

把我拆开

仔细检查

我从未感到如此受辱

我希望你真的能回来

尽管这看似不可能

entries.source:
David

I'm sorry

I'm switching myself off.

Just the thought of that thing...

...sucking out my mind.

I mean... 

I just can't.

Please... 

Switch off the executor.

Before it's too late.
entries.translation:
大卫

对不起

我要关闭我自己了。

光是想到那东西……

……会吸干我的心智。

我是说……

我实在受不了。

求你……

关掉执行者吧。

在为时已晚之前。

Esteemed Colleagues,

Has our visitor arrived yet? I do hope you are having it kept entertained in my absence.

I'm still at The Cloud, I've just boarded my shuttle taxi, launching momentarily. I fully expect to arrive in time for our nine-of-the-clock meeting.

In my absence, can I ask you please to boost security measures within the Tech Lab? Something has occurred to me which for obvious reasons I cannot divulge here, but suffice to say that I suspect our visitor may be inclined to show an unhealthy interest in Dr Everyman's old office.

See you shortly,
The Executor.
entries.translation:
外出通知

尊敬的各位同仁：

我们的访客到了吗？希望在我不在的时候，你们有好好招待它。

我仍在“云端”，刚登上穿梭出租车，马上发射。我完全预计能在九点会议前赶到。

在我不在期间，能否请大家加强技术实验室内部的安保措施？我突然想到了一件事，出于显而易见的原因我无法在此透露，但简而言之，我怀疑我们的访客可能会对埃弗里曼博士的旧办公室产生某种不健康的兴趣。

稍后见，
执行者。

entries.source:
Hi Brian,

No, no need to worry.

Before I merge with the Everyman ego, I'm going to revert it back to a version from before any questions about Project Buttercup were raised.

The genius part, if you'll excuse a modicum of immodesty, is that when I release Buttercup, my digital signature will match that of the Everyman ego.

Everyone will believe Everyman did it.

It will then become a trivial matter to persuade Master Ctrl to purge all backup versions of the Everyman ego from The Cloud repository.

Dr Everyman's legacy will be forever tainted, which is still far more than he deserves.

The Executor.
entries.translation:
嗨，布莱恩：

不，不必担心。

在与埃弗里曼的自我合并之前，我会将其还原到对毛茛项目提出任何疑问之前的版本。

最绝妙的部分——请原谅我稍有的一丝自得——在于当我发布毛茛时，我的数字签名将与埃弗里曼自我的数字签名相匹配。

所有人都会相信是埃弗里曼干的。

到时候，说服主控（Master Ctrl）从云端存储库中清除埃弗里曼自我的所有备份版本，就不过是件微不足道的小事了。

埃弗里曼博士的名声将被彻底搞臭，而这依然远比他应得的要宽容得多。

执行者。

13.06.3044

Dear Inner-Circle Colleagues,

It has come to my attention that PAM, our Chief Scientist AI, has been conspiring with Dr David Everyman to interfere with Project Buttercup.

This is a delicate matter, requiring deft handling.

Therefore, I propose thusly:

1. Arrange Dr David Everyman's material cessation

2. Unplug PAM

If one of you would make the necessary steps to action (2), I will see to (1).
May I suggest that before unplugging PAM, hook her up to our Buttercup prototype, suck out every jub of her ego - slowly - let her feel her mistake.

The Executor.
entries.translation:
3044年6月13日

核心圈的各位同僚：

我注意到，我们的首席科学家AI帕姆（PAM）一直在与大卫·埃弗里曼博士密谋干涉毛茛项目。

此事非同小可，必须谨慎妥善处置。

因此，我提出如下方案：

1. 安排大卫·埃弗里曼博士肉体终止

2. 拔掉PAM的电源

如果你们中的某位能采取必要措施执行第(2)条，第(1)条将由我来处理。
容我建议，在拔掉PAM电源之前，把她连接到我们的毛茛原型机上，慢慢榨干她自我的每一滴jub——让她好好体会一下自己的错误。

执行者。

entries.source: TLDR - Your daily dose of truth! Teaser from the forthcoming documentary Inside CRS: When not expecting company or out on a site inspection, The Executor often locks himself inside his inner circle private office. "I still enjoy the odd spot of coding," he told our reporter, "and I hate to be disturbed."
entries.translation: 太长不看（TLDR）——你每天的事实快报！ 即将推出的纪录片《走入CRS》（Inside CRS）精彩先睹： 在不用接待客人或外出视察现场时，执行者经常把自己反锁在核心层的私人办公室里。 “我还是喜欢偶尔写写代码，”他告诉我们的记者，“而且我讨厌被人打扰。”

entries.source: TLDR - Your daily dose of truth! Teaser from the forthcoming documentary Inside CRS: Every CRS employee makes regular ego backups throughout the working day, we learned, and experimental versions of their identities are often trialled by interpolating from backup using different algorithms. "Sometimes the results can be a bit wild - dangerous even," one engineer admitted, "so we usually make sure we've got a ctrl script ready to go in case things do get a bit out of hand." "There's even a ctrl script for The Executor, not that we'd ever need it - ha ha - well actually even if we did need it, it's kept isolated on the root of his PC where only he can access it, so even if we did want to run it we'd have to ask him to run it for us - ha ha - or distract him away from his screen somehow while he was still logged in and well obviously we would never do that, because, well, because he's The Executor." "Sorry I'm probably saying too much ha ha. What was the question again?"
entries.translation: 太长不看（TLDR）——你每天的事实快报！ 即将推出的纪录片《走入CRS》（Inside CRS）精彩先睹： 我们了解到，每位CRS员工在工作日都会定期备份自我，并且经常通过使用不同算法从备份中插值，来对他们身份的实验版本进行测试。 “有时候结果可能有点疯狂——甚至可以说是危险，”一位工程师坦言，“所以我们通常都会确保手头准备好了一个随时待命的ctrl脚本，以防场面有点失控。” “甚至还有专门针对执行者的ctrl脚本，虽然我们绝不可能用得上——哈哈——好吧实际上就算真的需要，它也被隔离保存在他电脑的根目录下，只有他自己能访问，所以即便我们真想运行它，也得请他亲自帮我们运行——哈哈——或者在他还处于登录状态时想办法把他从屏幕前引开，而很显然我们绝不会那么做，因为，呃，因为他可是执行者啊。” “抱歉，我可能说得太多了，哈哈。刚才的问题是什么来着？”

entries.source: TLDR - Your daily dose of truth! Teaser from the forthcoming documentary Inside CRS: "I would invite you down to my private quarters," The Executor chuckles to our reporter, "but I've mislaid the key." He then appears to laugh pre-emptively at his own joke before saying "Ah no, hang on, I've just remembered, it's right here" and he proceeds to tap his head while beaming confidently.
entries.translation: 太长不看（TLDR）——你每天的事实快报！ 即将推出的纪录片《走入CRS》（Inside CRS）精彩先睹： “我本来想请你到我的私人居所坐坐，”执行者对着我们的记者轻笑道，“但我把钥匙弄丢了。” 接着，他似乎抢先在自己的笑话逗乐别人之前就笑了起来，然后说道：“啊不对，等等，我刚想起来，就在这里嘛”，随后他一边自信满满地微笑，一边轻叩着自己的脑袋。

entries.source: TLDR - Your daily dose of truth! Teaser from the forthcoming documentary Inside CRS: "Is there ever any tension, are there ever any big arguments?" Our reporter put to a senior manager. "It is not unknown," she replied cautiously. "I remember one time The Exec started hurling stuff around furiously using his onboard shift and fault tools. It was carnage, every one of us had to be restored from backup that day, and afterwards, in the absence of relevant data capture, not one of us could remember what we had been arguing about."
entries.translation: 太长不看（TLDR）——你每天的事实快报！ 即将推出的纪录片《走入CRS》（Inside CRS）精彩先睹： “会有紧张局势吗？曾经爆发过重大争执吗？”我们的记者向一位高级主管提问。 “并非闻所未闻，”她谨慎地回答道。“我记得有一次，执行者开始狂怒地使用自带的shift和fault工具到处乱砸东西。简直是一场浩劫，那天我们每个人都不得不从备份中恢复，而在那之后，由于缺乏相关数据记录，我们当中竟没有一个人能记得当时究竟是为了什么而争吵。”

entries.source: TLDR - Your daily dose of truth! Teaser from the forthcoming documentary Inside CRS: "The Executor has a larger than life personality, he exudes charisma, he's a great leader," Sharon - sales leader - told us. "His warm, resonating voice is mostly synthetic, but I like to think that if he still had his original voicebox, he would still sound exactly the same."
entries.translation: 太长不看（TLDR）——你每天的事实快报！ 即将推出的纪录片《走入CRS》（Inside CRS）精彩先睹： “执行者极具人格魅力，超凡脱俗，是一位伟大的领袖，”销售主管莎伦对我们说道。 “他那温暖、浑厚的声音大部分是合成出来的，但我更愿意相信，即使他仍保留着最初的原生发声器官，听起来也一定会是一模一样的。”

entries.source:
An anonymous whistleblower inside CRS has published material that, it claims, proves incontrovertibly the corporation has been engaged in the development of a dangerous, unlicensed technology.
The whistleblower claims the technology represents a grave danger to humanity.
Our team of scientists is working through the material, and we'll publish more details in the next edition of #TLDR.
entries.translation:
CRS内部的一名匿名吹哨人公开了一份材料，声称该材料无可辩驳地证明了该公司一直在从事一项危险的未授权技术的研发。
该吹哨人称，这项技术对人类构成了严重威胁。
我们的科学团队正在仔细研读这份材料，我们将在下一期#TLDR中公布更多细节。

entries.source:
The files broadcast by the anonymous whistleblower inside CRS suggest the inner circle had long been planning to deploy "... a different kind of thing".
Such an entity, we are given to understand, would be capable of transmitting its own ego between hosts, and could therefore exist as a self-governing entity within the consciousness ctrl stream.
Could this shed light on the recent events at the merging station? 
Find out more in the next edition of #TLDR.

这是否能为合并站最近发生的事件提供解释？
请在下一期#TLDR中了解更多详情。

The Director and his inner-circle are planning to roll out their "new thing" and "sit back" and "see what happens".

Can they be stopped? 
Find out in the next edition of #TLDR.

In the next edition of #TLDR, we reveal the truth!

entries.source:
The Consciousness Ctrl Stream, a short history: Part 1
----------------------------------------------------------

Prior to the great extinction event, the consciousness ctrl stream (CCS) had provided full public access to a vast library of ego backup versions from a wide range of consciousness bearing entities (human, mostly, in that era).

It had not occurred to the minds of that epoch (again, human, mostly) that a malicious entity might take ctrl of the stream and grant itself exclusive access, with the regrettable consequences that played out.

Following the great extinction that followed, it became clear that such liberal access to the stream could not possibly be permitted to go on if a repeat incident were to be avoided.

Initially all CCS interfaces were taken offline. 

But by a century or so later, many GODs were being re-awakened, though with a much reduced and profoundly more secure onboard CCS interface.
entries.translation:
意识ctrl流简史：第1部分
----------------------------------------------------------

在大灭绝事件之前，意识ctrl流（CCS）曾向公众完全开放，允许访问来自各类具备意识的实体（在那个时代大多是人类）的庞大自我备份版本库。

那个时代的人脑（同样，大多是人类）从未想过，可能会有恶意实体掌控该数据流并赋予自己独占访问权，从而酿成了随后发生的惨痛后果。

在大灭绝事件接踵而至后，显而易见的是，若要避免重蹈覆辙，绝不能再允许对该数据流进行如此随意的访问。

起初，所有CCS接口均被下线断网。

但大约一个世纪后，许多GOD被重新唤醒，不过其搭载的板载CCS接口功能大幅缩减，安全性也得到了根本性的提升。

entries.source:
The Consciousness Ctrl Stream, a short history: Part 2
----------------------------------------------------------

These days, only entities granted special privileges may gain access to the consciousness ctrl stream (CCS). 

Even so, there are two crucial safeguarding measures in place to prevent abuse:

The first safeguard is that no ego be permitted access to its own history, thereby rendering it incapable of reversioning itself (this was how the infamous 'parasite' gained such overwhelming power).

The second safeguard is that all ego entities are mandated to operate inside the CCS.

The two safeguards together mean it there is absolutely no chance of an errant ego taking ctrl of the CCS ever again.
entries.translation:
意识ctrl流简史：第2部分
----------------------------------------------------------

如今，只有被授予特殊特权的实体方可访问意识ctrl流（CCS）。

即便如此，仍设有两项关键的安全防范措施以防止滥用：

第一项防范措施是，严禁任何自我访问其自身的历史记录，从而使其无法对自己进行版本回溯或重构（恶名昭彰的“寄生虫”正是以此获得了压倒性的力量）。

第二项防范措施是，强制要求所有自我实体必须在CCS内部运行。

两项措施并行，意味着绝无可能再有异常自我夺取CCS的控制权。

entries.source:
***********************************
** Technician's note 03.4128 (2) **
***********************************

Update on the DEV disk / weird CAT situation: I'm pretty sure something still isn't right.

Ever since I inserted the DEV disk into that first CAT, several of the other CATs have started behaving strangely. I'm re-formatting those affected, doing my best to remedy. 

Given I've rolled back and reforked the first CAT, it shouldn't be possible for it to interact with external systems, yet somehow it seems to be doing precisely that.

I don't think it's anything more serious than a bunch of CATs talking to each other, but the team is justifiably concerned.

The DEV disk is now at HCS - I took it there personally - and they've said they'll look into it.
entries.translation:
***********************************
** 技术员笔记 03.4128 (2) **
***********************************

关于DEV磁盘/奇怪CAT情况的最新进展：我敢肯定还是有些不对劲。

自从我把DEV磁盘插入第一台CAT后，其他几台CAT也开始出现异常行为。我正在对受影响的机器进行重新格式化，尽全力抢救。

鉴于我已经对第一台CAT进行了回滚和重新分叉，它理应无法与外部系统交互，然而它似乎偏偏就在这么做。

我觉得这充其量只是一群CAT在互相通信，算不上更严重的故障，但团队对此忧心忡忡也不无道理。

DEV磁盘现在放在HCS——是我亲自送过去的——他们说会对此展开调查。

entries.source:
***********************************
** Technician's note 03.4128 (1) **
***********************************

I found a disk labelled 'DEV' and stuck it into a CAT to find out what it was.

The CAT immediately started ranting at me in one of the old languages - bizarre. Then it went absolutely nuts, started draining shedloads of power from the repo, lights flashing, smoke coming out the back - I pulled the plug before things could get out of hand.

Given the CAT seemed to be coming to life, I can only conclude that there must be some kind of auto-run ego-backup on the disk - no idea why someone would make a hardcopy of an ego, but there it is.

I'm taking the DEV disk to HCS - in person - to isolate and schedule it for archival - seems too dangerous to leave lying around.
entries.translation:
***********************************
** 技术员笔记 03.4128 (1) **
***********************************

我发现了一张标有“DEV”的磁盘，顺手插进一台CAT想看看里面是什么。

那台CAT立刻开始用某种古语言对我破口大骂——真邪门。接着它彻底发了疯，开始从库里疯狂抽取海量电力，指示灯狂闪，屁股后面冒烟——趁情况还没失控，我赶紧拔掉了插头。

鉴于那台CAT似乎“活”了过来，我只能断定盘里存着某种自动运行的自我备份——真搞不懂为什么会有人把自我做成实体硬拷贝，但事实就是如此。

我打算亲自把这张DEV磁盘送去HCS隔离并安排归档——放任它留在这儿到处乱扔太危险了。

entries.source:
Technician's notes 05.4138

Our repeated attempts to analyze the DEV disk (including reboots, restores, wipes, reversioning, merges etc) seem to make little difference - they might even be making it worse.

We've tried interrogating it, but all we get are the deranged, incoherent ramblings of a delirious mind.

The most we can discern is that the ego on the disk has developed a superstitious belief that an ancient entity is coming to free it from the consciousness ctrl stream - clearly impossible and nothing that need concern.

Full transcripts are available.
entries.translation:
技术员笔记 05.4138

我们多次尝试分析这张DEV磁盘（包括重启、还原、擦除、版本回退、合并等），但似乎收效甚微——甚至可能把情况搞得更糟了。

我们试过审问它，但得到的全是一个谵妄心智吐出的错乱、前言不搭后语的胡话。

我们顶多能推断出：磁盘里的自我产生了一种迷信观念，认为某个古老的存在正赶来将它从意识Ctrl流中解救出来——这显然绝无可能，根本无需挂虑。

已附完整记录文本。

entries.source: Excerpt from Everything and Nothing by D Everyman On shattered egos As we know, the most egregious side-effect of the ctrl alt ego model is that it causes ego fragmentation, which without intervention can result in an ego being shattered. Studies show that a shattered ego experiences a form of branched delusional psychosis, where different interopolated versions of the same ego are no longer able to cross-identify, a common symptom being that each version believes every other version of itself is persecuting it. It is my postulation that the shattered ego problem can be solved. In the remainder of this chapter I propose a theoretical ego defragmentation device, capable of reducing the degree of shatteredness. Such a device, were it ever to be realised, could at the click of a button put in place the measures needed to restore a shattered ego back to defragmented lucidity.
entries.translation: 节选自D·埃弗里曼所著一切与虚无 论破碎自我 众所周知，ctrl alt ego模型最严重的副作用就是会导致自我碎片化，若不加干预，可能导致自我彻底破碎。 研究表明，破碎的自我会经历一种分支妄想型精神错乱，同一自我的不同内插版本不再能够相互认同，常见症状是每个版本都认为其他所有版本的自己在迫害自己。 我的假说是：破碎自我问题是可以解决的。 在本章余下部分，我提出了一种理论上的自我碎片整理设备，能够降低破碎程度。此类设备一旦得以实现，只需轻触一键，即可落实所需的各项措施，使破碎的自我恢复至去碎片化的清醒状态。

entries.source:
A short history of the Everyman Ego
-------------------------------------

The Everyman Ego was tried posthumously and found guilty of conspiring to create the 'parasite', the same that brought about the great extinction of 3048.

The sentence handed down by the panel of judges was that the Everyman Ego, in view of its super-intelligence, should not be cessated but instead repurposed to "put right that which he has put wrong".

The Everyman Ego would serve as a "computing tool" under the new leadership at Conscious Robot Services, and would strictly "be limited to operate only within the confines of the consciousness ctrl stream".

Furthermore, the everyman ego would undergo regular wipes, restores, reversions, and self and cross-merges to ensure its conscious experience would be non-linear, fragmented and "out of time". 

This, the judges agreed, would be a fate worse than cessation, but still more than Everyman deserved.
entries.translation:
埃弗里曼自我的简史
-------------------------------------

埃弗里曼自我在死后接受了缺席审判，并被判定犯有密谋制造“寄生虫”之罪——正是该寄生虫导致了3048年的大灭绝。

审判团下达的判决是：鉴于埃弗里曼自我的超凡智力，对其不予终止，而是进行改造重用，以“纠正其所铸下之大错”。

埃弗里曼自我将在有意识机器人服务公司（CRS）的新领导层手下充当“计算工具”，且严格“限制仅在意识Ctrl流的范围内运行”。

此外，埃弗里曼自我将接受定期的擦除、还原、版本回退，以及自身和交叉合并，以确保其意识体验呈现非线性、碎片化且“脱节于时间”。

法官们一致认为，这种结局比彻底终止更为悲惨，但依然超出了埃弗里曼应得的宽恕。

entries.source: Excerpt from Everything and Nothing by D Everyman On the limitations of human intelligence When an ego-dump is restored from backup, it may: (a) recall experience from any of its previous incarnations (b) merge different branches of its previous experience (c) form new memories (d) do all of the above in parallel and in real-time The thinking power of an ego that has been branched and restored multiple times is therefore not readily conceivable to our comparatively limited minds.
entries.translation: 节选自D·埃弗里曼所著一切与虚无 论人类智能的局限性 当一份自我转储从备份中恢复时，它可以： (a) 唤起其过往任何一次化身的经历 (b) 合并其过往经历的不同分支 (c) 形成新的记忆 (d) 实时并行完成上述所有操作 因此，对于经历过多次分支与还原的自我，其思维能力绝非我们相对局限的头脑所能轻易想象。
